slides.label: B
slides.sectionTitle: Where we meet sustainability in the real world
slides.sectionPrompt: Four quick trust checks, one per slide

slides.text: “SHEIN continues to push more responsible and circular production practices, both within the organization and for the overall industry, to positively contribute to the resilience of nature and the empowerment of local communities.”
slides.question: Gut reaction, no right answers: how much do you trust this?
slides.sectionTitle: Where we meet sustainability in the real world
slides.revealText: Italy’s competition authority fined Shein €1m in 2025 for misleading green claims, including claims about circularity.

slides.text: To become “a net-zero emissions energy business” by 2050.
slides.question: Gut reaction, no right answers: how much do you trust this?
slides.sectionTitle: Where we meet sustainability in the real world
slides.revealText: in March 2024 Shell weakened its 2030 target. It changed a 20% cut in carbon intensity to a range of 15–20%. It dropped its 2035 target altogether, citing “uncertainty in the pace of change”. The 2050 goal remains, but Shell warns there is “significant risk” it may not meet it.

slides.text: New petrol and diesel cars will no longer be sold from 2030.
slides.question: Gut reaction, no right answers: how much do you trust this?
slides.sectionTitle: Where we meet sustainability in the real world
slides.revealText: in September 2023, Rishi Sunak pushed it back to 2035.

slides.text: “We exist to end exploitation in the cocoa industry.”
slides.question: Gut reaction, no right answers: how much do you trust this?
slides.sectionTitle: Where we meet sustainability in the real world
slides.revealText: Tony’s reports much lower child labour in its long-term partner communities. The figures are its own, and the goal isn’t reached yet.
